message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'src/**'
      - 'package.json'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: docs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: docs/package-lock.json
      # The tuning pages import the library from src/, so its dependencies
      # must be installed at the repository root too.
      - run: npm install --ignore-scripts
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v6
        with:
          enablement: true
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/out

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5",
  "rationale": "The workflow has no explicit job timeout, so a runaway job could consume the default 360-minute limit. The repository CI history shows representative successful runs completing in roughly 1 minute, satisfying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition (representative successful-duration history exists). Adding explicit timeouts with operational headroom (10 min for the build job that installs dependencies and runs next build; 5 min for the fast pages deploy) bounds runaway consumption without changing any build/test step, permission, or deployment behavior, preserving required coverage. Dependency caching is already present via setup-node cache: npm, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated (equivalent cache already exists), and P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated because this is a GitHub Pages deployment workflow (release/deployment work).",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
